ledger.note: March 1867: Raja Mahdi seizes Klang and defies the Selangor court. 'In March 1867, Raja Mahdi captured the fort of Klang'; the quarrel began in 1866 when Raja Abdullah authorised traders to collect opium taxes in the Klang Valley and Mahdi refused to pay.
March 1870: Klang is lost. Raja Ismail and Tengku Kudin 'laid siege to Klang City' and Mahdi 'withdrew north to Kuala Selangor'.
March 1870: Mahdi's base moves to Kuala Selangor, which the page has him holding 1870-1871.
July 1871: the British capture Kuala Selangor after a pirate attack traced to Mahdi's stronghold and give it to Kudin.
1872: Mahdi takes Kuala Lumpur, which is razed.
1872: Kuala Selangor is 'recaptured by Mahdi's forces'.
March 1873: Kudin's men with Pahangese fighters defeat Syed Mashhor, Mahdi's ally, in Kuala Lumpur.
8 November 1873: Pahangese forces capture Kuala Selangor; fighting 'largely ended'.
November 1873: the faction holds no land. Raja Mahdi 'went into exile in 1874' (page); the dissolve is dated to the last town lost.

wars.name: Selangor Civil War
wars.outcome: Mahdi's faction lost every town it held by 8 November 1873 and Mahdi went into exile in 1874.
wars.note: Same war as in the sultanate-of-selangor dossier; 'lasted from 1866 to 1874' (page). Years clipped by the reviewer (se-03-a, 2026-10-19) to the faction's life: the war ran 1866-1874 on the page, but Mahdi's faction held land only from March 1867 (Klang) to 8 November 1873 (Kuala Selangor); the full span stays in the sultanate-of-selangor dossier.

certainty.note: Town territories of a few days' control; the page names places, not frontiers.

sources.title: Selangor Civil War
sources.note: Every date and place; Mahdi held Klang 1867-1870, Kuala Selangor 1870-1871 and 1872, Kuala Lumpur 1872.

notes: Rebel dossier added by se-03-a for the Selangor Civil War, as the brief allows for rebel states that held land for a year or more (Klang, March 1867 to March 1870). Cliopatria has no row. The page does not call Mahdi's party a state; it is a faction holding towns, so the shapes are town discs (Klang 15 km, Kuala Selangor 15 km at lon 101.249 lat 3.344, Kuala Lumpur 12 km), researcher estimates. Allies on Mahdi's side named by the page: Syed Mashhor. The other side: Tengku Kudin (viceroy from the Sultan, 1867/1868), Raja Ismail, Pahang (about 1,000 men), the British (July 1871). Raja Abdullah, the Klang holder dispossessed by Mahdi, died in Malacca (date not given). Gazetteer name needed: Kuala Selangor.
